learn.title: Sorting an array
learn.body: Sorting puts items in order, here smallest first. Sorted data makes binary search possible and makes many other tasks easier. Bubble sort is the simplest idea: compare neighbours and swap them when they are in the wrong order.

learn.title: One pass over {5, 1, 4, 2, 8}
learn.body: Walk along the array and compare each pair of neighbours.
steps: Compare 5 and 1: wrong order, swap. Array: 1 5 4 2 8
Compare 5 and 8: fine. The largest item, 8, is at the end

learn.title: Why it is called bubble
learn.body: After pass 1 the largest item has bubbled to the end, and it is in its final place. After pass 2 the second largest is in place, and so on. So each pass can stop one item earlier than the last.

learn.title: Bubble sort in C
learn.body: `p` is the last index still in play, and it shrinks each pass. The `if` swaps a neighbour pair using a temporary variable `t`.

learn.title: The cost
learn.body: Pass 1 makes 4 comparisons for 5 items, then 3, 2 and 1. That is 10 in total, or $n(n-1)/2$ for n items. This code does that many comparisons whatever the order of the input, so it is $\Theta(n^2)$.
A swap needs a third variable. Writing `a[i] = a[i + 1]` first would lose the old value of `a[i]`.

questions.prompt: What does one bubble sort pass do to the largest unsorted item?
choices: It moves it to the end of the unsorted part
It moves it to the front
It leaves it where it is
questions.explanation: Swapping neighbours carries the largest value along until it reaches the end.

questions.prompt: After the first full pass on `{5, 1, 4, 2, 8}`, what is the last item?
questions.explanation: 8 is the largest. It was already at the end, and nothing is bigger.

questions.prompt: After pass 1 on `{5, 1, 4, 2, 8}`, the array is...
questions.explanation: 5 swapped past 1, 4 and 2, then stopped at 8.

questions.prompt: To swap `a[i]` and `a[i + 1]` safely you need a \_\_ variable.
questions.explanation: Without a temporary, the first assignment would overwrite a value you still need.

questions.prompt: How many comparisons does this bubble sort make for 5 items? (4 + 3 + 2 + 1)
questions.explanation: The passes make 4, 3, 2 and 1 comparisons: 10 in total, which is $n(n-1)/2$.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of one bubble sort pass in order.
steps: Swap them if the left one is bigger
Move one place right and repeat to the end of the pass
questions.explanation: A pass is a left to right walk of compare and maybe swap.

questions.prompt: What is the big O of this bubble sort?
questions.explanation: Two nested loops over about n items each.
